name: Tiangong space station (2022- three-module configuration)
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'Tiangong' type. Body frame: +X along velocity (Tianhe's axis, forward node), +Y starboard (Wentian), +Z nadir; origin at the centre of Tianhe's docking node. Three groups: the station, alpha (the labs' rear booms about the labs' axis) and beta (each wing about its long axis - two pivots). Visiting Shenzhou/Tianzhou, Tianhe's small wings, the robotic arms and radiators are omitted. Attitude and every material are estimates.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: flown like the ISS: +X (Tianhe's axis, node forward) along velocity, +Z nadir, labs along the orbit normal
sources.source: No published flight attitude found. With the labs' arrays turning about the labs' common axis (below), that axis must lie across the orbit plane to track the Sun once per orbit; Tianhe's forward/nadir/aft ports serve visiting vehicles (Wikipedia, Tianhe). Estimate.

sources.subject: station
sources.value: root group: Tianhe + the two laboratory modules in a T
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Tiangong space station' / 'Tianhe core module' / 'Wentian module' (accessed 2026-09-24): 'T-shaped', Wentian starboard and Mengtian port of Tianhe's forward docking hub.

sources.subject: alpha
sources.value: each lab's rear boom turns about the labs' common axis, tracking the Sun (first of the arrays' two axes)
sources.source: China Space Report, 'Tiangong' (chinaspacereport.wordpress.com): the lab modules' wings are 'two-axis steerable to track the Sun', 'mounted on a large boom with its centre attached to the rear end of the module'. Assigning the first axis to the module axis (as the ISS SARJ) is DERIVED from that layout.

sources.subject: beta
sources.value: each wing turns about its own long axis (second axis); the two wings of a lab share one line (2 pivots)
sources.source: China Space Report, 'Tiangong' (chinaspacereport.wordpress.com) (two-axis steerable). Axis assignment derived, as for alpha.

sources.subject: tianhe_node
sources.value: 2.8 m sphere at Tianhe's forward end; range 2.5-3.0 m
sources.source: eoPortal, 'Tiangong Space Station': Tianhe = 'the node cabin, the life control cabin, which is divided into the large and small column segments, and the resource cabin'. Section sizes are not published; node and small column taken at ~2.8 m.

sources.value: 4.0 m x 2.8 m small column + 9.8 m x 4.2 m large column/resource cabin: 16.6 m overall with the node
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Tiangong space station' / 'Tianhe core module' / 'Wentian module' (accessed 2026-09-24) and eoPortal, 'Tiangong Space Station': total length 16.6 m, maximum diameter 4.2 m. The split between sections is an estimate (range +-1.5 m).

sources.value: 17.9 m x 4.2 m each, docked 0.4 m off the node
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Tiangong space station' / 'Tianhe core module' / 'Wentian module' (accessed 2026-09-24): both 17.9 m long, 4.2 m diameter. Station 'diameter ~39 m' = the two labs end to end (39.4 m here).

sources.value: 1 x 1 x 3 m box at each lab's rear end
sources.source: China Space Report, 'Tiangong' (chinaspacereport.wordpress.com): 'a large boom with its centre attached to the rear end of the module'. Size not published.

sources.value: four 27 x 4.1 m flexible wings (110 m2 each), two per lab, 57.6 m tip to tip
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Tiangong space station' / 'Tianhe core module' / 'Wentian module' (accessed 2026-09-24) (Wentian) and eoPortal, 'Tiangong Space Station': each lab's pair has a 'wingspan of over 55 m and an energy collection area of 110 m2' per array; Space.com: each array 'nearly 30 m long'. Width = area / length (derived). Flexible GaAs arrays: solar_cell_flex / solar_array_flex_back (backlit transmission) - estimate for the substrate. Tianhe's own two small one-axis wings are OMITTED: CMSE's design moves them to the labs' short trusses once the labs arrive; where they are now is unverified.

sources.subject: cn_module_blanket
sources.value: diffuse albedo 0.6, white thermal blankets; range 0.45-0.8
sources.source: Tiangong's modules appear white in CMSE imagery; no published reflectance.

sources.subject: boom_metal
sources.value: albedo 0.3, F0 0.3, roughness 0.45 (the ISS truss material)
